transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hey, thanks. Yeah, um, I guess the main thing is I just get pulled off track by every little sound or thought. Like, I’ll be trying to work on a job application... which reminds me, I was looking at this one for a warehouse earlier today. My buddy Dave works there and he says the hours are kind of garbage, but they have those free mango energy drinks in the breakroom. Man, those things are so good, but they totally mess up my stomach if I drink them too fast, you know? 

Anyway, wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, why I'm here. So I'll be sitting there trying to finish the application, and then a car drives by outside, or my phone buzzes, or just some random idea pops into my head, and suddenly I'm off doing something completely different before I even notice I stopped working on what I was supposed to be doing.
Aside from getting distracted easily, do you also often feel physically restless or have trouble staying still?

Yeah, totally. It's like I have this nervous energy all the time. Honestly, since I can't play soccer like I used to—which, man, I miss it so much. We had this Sunday league team, the River Rats, and we were actually pretty decent. We made it to the finals two years ago, but then our goalie moved to Texas for some tech job, and it just fell apart. Texas is crazy hot anyway, I don't know how he deals with it. 

But yeah, since I'm not running around on the pitch anymore, just sitting around the house makes me feel like I'm literally crawling out of my skin. I can't just chill on the couch. I end up just pacing from room to room, picking things up and putting them down. It drives my mom crazy when I do it in the kitchen while she's trying to cook. She makes this killer lasagna, by the way, with like three different kinds of cheese. But yeah, sitting still is... it's rough.
Did you experience similar problems with staying focused or sitting still back when you were in elementary school?

Oh, man, yeah. Elementary school was... it was a whole thing. I remember my teachers were always moving my desk around. Like, they'd put me right up next to their desk, or in the back corner, because I was always blurting things out or talking to whoever was next to me. Which reminds me, my best friend in third grade, Tyler, he had this huge collection of those crazy bones toys. Do you remember those? They were like these little plastic alien things you'd flick at each other. We got in so much trouble for playing with them during math. Tyler's actually a plumber now, makes really good money. 

But yeah, school. I was always forgetting my homework, like, leaving it on the kitchen table or just straight up losing it in my backpack. My backpack was like a black hole. And whenever we had worksheets, I'd just blast through them so I could go play, but I'd make all these stupid careless mistakes. My mom used to get so mad because she knew I knew the answers, I just wouldn't slow down. She tried color-coding my folders once, which lasted about two days before I lost the red one on the bus. That bus driver, Mr. Henderson, he was always yelling at us... wait, did I answer the question? Yeah, I've always been like this, basically.
Have you ever had periods lasting several days where you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt fully energized?

No, I don't think so. I mean, my sleep is usually pretty normal, unless I'm just staying up late playing video games or something. I've been playing this new open-world game, actually, and it's insane. The map is huge, like, it takes an hour just to ride a horse from one side to the other. My buddy Dave—the one who works at the warehouse—he's been playing it too, but he always plays as a mage, which I think is kind of a cheap way to play because you just stand back and shoot fireballs. I always go for the melee builds, you know? Get right in there with a big sword. It's way more intense. 

But yeah, sleep. No, I don't really have days where I don't sleep and feel totally fine. If I don't get enough sleep, I'm usually pretty draggy the next day. I'll need like three cups of coffee just to function, and even then, I'm just kind of staring at the wall. My mom's coffee maker is this ancient thing from the 90s, and it takes forever to brew, so half the time I just end up going to the gas station down the street. They have this hazelnut cream that's pretty good, but sometimes the guy working there forgets to restock it. So yeah, I definitely need my sleep.
Do you often find yourself worrying excessively about various everyday things, like your finances, health, or family?

Worrying? Uh, not really. I mean, I don't have a job right now, so my finances are basically nonexistent, but I don't sit around stressing over it. My mom definitely does enough of that for both of us. She's always on me about it, sending me links to jobs, like... the other day she sent me this one for a dog walking app. Which actually sounds pretty awesome because I love dogs. 

My neighbor has this huge golden retriever, Buster, and he is the absolute goofiest dog. Whenever I walk past their fence, he brings me a shoe. Like, not a dog toy, just a random shoe he stole from their porch. One time it was this giant muddy rain boot, and I had to awkwardly hand it back to the neighbor over the fence. The neighbor is this older guy, always wearing these loud Hawaiian shirts even in the winter. He's got a whole collection of them. 

But wait, what were you asking? Oh, worrying. Yeah, no, I don't really get super anxious about my health or money or anything like that. I just kind of take things as they come.
Do you use any recreational drugs or drink alcohol?

Drugs or alcohol? Uh, no, not really. I don't do any drugs, and I don't really drink. I mean, sometimes my mom buys those hard seltzers, the black cherry ones? But they taste like TV static to me. I'd rather just have a Coke. 

Actually, I drink way too much soda. Cherry Coke is the best, but you can't always find it in the cans, usually just the plastic bottles. And the bottles get warm too fast if you don't drink them right away. I had this idea once to make a mini-fridge that you could plug directly into your Xbox, so you wouldn't even have to get up to get a cold drink while you're playing. You could just reach over. I even started sketching it out in this notebook I have, but I couldn't figure out the cooling mechanism. I ended up watching like three hours of YouTube videos on how refrigerators work. Did you know it's all about compressing gas? It's actually pretty crazy. The guy in the video explaining it had this wild mustache, looked exactly like the Pringles guy. I haven't had Pringles in forever... 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, drinking. Yeah, no, I don't drink or do drugs. Just not my thing.
